hypothesis: For the exact historical fast/segment/document hierarchy, segment-parallel Jacobi (multiple-shooting) sweeps reach the sequential reference to a 1e-6 boundary-input residual in fewer than 16 sweeps at T=1024 (N=32 segments) on the trained 120M checkpoint, so the sequential loop over segments that FastHierarchy leaves could be replaced by a few batched sweeps without changing the equations.
primary_comparator: Token-by-token HierarchicalDistributionStudent.transition from the recovered byte-exact source (unchanged), which FastHierarchy matched at FP64 1e-9 in matched-scratch-fineweb-20261017-v1.
primary_metric: K(1e-6): sweeps until every guessed boundary input (fast state entering each segment, segment state, document state used as fast input) changes by <= 1e-6 absolute in FP64; max over the three PRIMARY rows of PLAN.json. Reported with the true max |hidden - reference| at that sweep.
minimum_useful_effect: K(1e-6) < 16 at T=1024. Break-even under the favorable cost model: a sweep costs at most two reference segment iterations (~1.0 ms vs ~0.50 ms per segment iteration inferred from the matched-scratch H100 B=1 table), so 32 iterations ~16 ms equal 16 sweeps. Minimum possible K is 2 (one sweep plus one verifying sweep).
success_rule: Advance to a GPU latency proposal only if max K(1e-6) < 16 on the PRIMARY rows AND every row's wavefront check passes (segments 0..k-1 within the parity tolerance after sweep k) AND the hidden error at convergence (residual 1e-12) is <= 1e-9 in FP64 AND the failure control fails parity. CPU timings are not speed evidence.
futility_rule: Stop this line if max K(1e-6) >= 16 on the PRIMARY rows: record the obstruction (slow-state or fast-state sensitivity) and do not lower the target. Stop and report a defect if any wavefront check fails or the positive control fails.

design.mechanism_equations: Unchanged reference equations. Sweep k: given guesses Hin_j (fast state entering segment j), S_j, D_floor(j/8), run fast GRU over all N segments as one batch (input projection split as W_tok e_t + W_seg S_j + W_doc D + b, same GRUCell gates); Hin_{j+1} <- last fast state of segment j; S_{i+1} = segment_cell(mean_i, S_i) for i=0..N-1; D_m = document_cell(S_{8m}, D_{m-1}); hidden = combine([fast, S, D]) with the last token of segment j using S_{j+1}, D_floor((j+1)/8). Cold start: all guesses zero. Wavefront: segment 0 always has exact inputs, so after sweep k segments 0..k-1 are exact; N sweeps reproduce the reference.
design.control_rationale: Positive control: small-width default init must converge and pass hidden parity. Failure control: a deliberately wrong last-token slow-state rule must fail hidden parity, showing the verifier catches the plausible indexing defect. Favorable (default init), saturated (x3, as parity64.py) and adversarial long-memory (z-bias +4) synthetic rows bracket the trained rows.
